# Local Review

> Local Review (npm: `local-review`) is a local, GitHub-PR-style review UI for a stack of git commits, run with `npx local-review` and served at http://localhost:5622. Each commit is a candidate PR, reviewed before anything is pushed. Projects, PR text and review comments are plain YAML files that a coding agent reads and writes. This file tells an agent how to create a Local Review project (a project definition, `project.yaml`) for the user.

**This is the docs site's copy.** If Local Review is running, read http://localhost:5622/llms.txt instead (or the port the user gave):
the same file for the version they run, plus the actual data directory, the existing projects and URLs for that port.
`npx local-review` starts it; `npx local-review guide` prints the full agent guide without it.
By default the data directory is `~/.local-review` (or `$LOCAL_REVIEW_HOME`), and projects are `~/.local-review/projects/<slug>/project.yaml`.

**The rules:**

- **Reviewed repos are read-only.** Local Review never commits to, checks out, rebases, fetches or pushes the repos it shows; setting up a project needs only read-only git (`log`, `merge-base`, `rev-parse`).
- **Comments are never imported from GitHub.** Local Review's review threads are between the reviewer and the agent, locally. Don't copy GitHub review comments, threads or PR descriptions into it, and don't send its threads to GitHub.
- **Never delete or replace user data.** Create new files under the projects directory; never overwrite an existing `project.yaml` or remove anything there. `local-review init` only ever creates.
- **Don't push, open PRs or touch GitHub** while setting up. That comes later, and only when the reviewer says so (the agent guide).

**How to set up a project** (the "Setting up a project" section of the agent guide):

When the reviewer asks you to set up a project for their work (say, "the feature-xyz branch of ~/code/my-service"):

1. **Look at the repo, read-only.** Find the branch and what it's based on, then list the commits in the range,
   oldest first: `git -C ~/code/my-service log --reverse --format='%h %s' origin/main..feature-xyz`. Each commit
   will be one PR. Don't commit, rebase, check out or push anything while you set up: Local Review never modifies
   the repos it shows, and neither should setting it up. Reshaping the commits is a separate job, done only when
   the reviewer asks (the agent guide's "Building the local representation").
2. **Pick a slug** for the project: letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, not starting with `.`, e.g. `feature-xyz`.
   It's the project's directory name and its URL, http://localhost:5622/feature-xyz. Choose one that isn't taken
   (`curl -s http://localhost:5622/api/projects | jq -r '.projects[].slug'` lists them, or look in the projects
   directory).
3. **Write `<projects>/<slug>/project.yaml`**: one entry in `repos` per repo, with its `path`, `branch` and `base`.
   Either run `local-review init <slug>` and edit the commented example it writes, or create the file yourself; never
   replace or edit an existing project's file to make a new one. Group the commits into `stacks` only if the
   reviewer asked for stacks or the commits fall into obvious groups; with no `stacks:`, the whole range is one
   stack, named after the branch. A `title` is enough; leave `description` (the project intro) out unless the
   reviewer asks for one.
4. **Create nothing else.** `prs/` and `reviews/` fill in as the review happens: never pre-create them, and never
   import comments, threads or PR descriptions from GitHub (Local Review's threads are only ever written in Local
   Review, by the reviewer and you).
5. **Check it.** `local-review plan <slug>` prints the PRs and any warnings (a missing branch, a bad selector), and
   works without the server. With the server running, `curl -s http://localhost:5622/api/projects/<slug>` shows the
   commits, and any `error` or `warnings`, for the project and for each repo. The server picks the new file up
   live: no restart.
6. **Tell the reviewer the URL**, http://localhost:5622/<slug>, and how many PRs and stacks it shows.

The full schema is [project.yaml](https://local-review.edspencer.net/reference/project-yaml.md); the commented example
that `init` writes is
[examples/project.example.yaml](https://github.com/edspencer/local-review/blob/main/examples/project.example.yaml).

**The commented example project** (what `npx local-review init <slug>` writes):

```yaml
# A Local Review project. `npx local-review init my-feature` creates one like this, in
# ~/.local-review/projects/my-feature/project.yaml (or under $LOCAL_REVIEW_HOME/projects/);
# it is also a commented reference for writing one by hand.
#
# Edit the paths and branches below. The directory name ("my-feature") is the project's slug, used in
# URLs: http://localhost:5622/my-feature. Edits are picked up live, no restart needed.
# The full schema and the stack selector rules: https://local-review.edspencer.net/reference/project-yaml/
title: My feature
description: |                        # optional: the project intro (Markdown), editable in the UI too.
  One or two paragraphs of context for the whole effort. "Copy full PR body" puts it at the top of
  every PR's body, followed by the stack note and then the PR's own description.
repos:
  - path: ~/code/my-service           # a local clone; it is only ever read, never modified
    # name: my-service                # optional, default: the path's basename (used in URLs and dir names)
    branch: me/my-feature             # range end = this branch's head (or `to: <sha|ref>`, inclusive)
    base: origin/main                 # range start = merge-base(base, end), exclusive; default origin/HEAD, main, master
    # from: <sha|ref>                 # alternative start: the first commit included (overrides base)
    # landed: ["0a1b2c3d"]            # after merges: PRs frozen by the agent, bottom to top (prs file keys; see
                                      # https://local-review.edspencer.net/concepts/landed-prs/). They come first
                                      # and keep their numbers.
    stacks:                           # optional; consecutive groups of commits, in order
      - title: Groundwork
        color: blue                   # blue green purple orange pink teal red, or "#hex"; default cycles (yellow is
                                      # reserved for follow-on stacks)
        # no starts_at: the first stack starts at the first commit
      - title: The feature itself
        color: green
        starts_at: "Add the feature flag"   # a commit subject (survives rebases) or a quoted sha prefix
        # optional: a note for this stack (Markdown), how it relates to the others. It comes after the
        # intro in each of this stack's full PR bodies.
        description: |
          Builds on Groundwork.
      - title: Later
        starts_at: "Polish the feature"
        follow_on: true               # optional: parked work, shown yellow and faded, left out of totals and of
                                      # `local-review plan` by default. Advisory only; keep follow-on stacks at the end.
                                      # Always yellow: a `color:` here is ignored.
  # More repos can follow, each with its own range and stacks:
  # - path: ~/code/my-client
  #   branch: me/my-feature
```

## Docs

- [Agent guide](https://local-review.edspencer.net/agents/agent-guide.md): the whole guide for agents (the data model, the HTTP API, review threads, fixups, branches, publishing as GitHub stacked PRs, merges). Also `npx local-review guide`.
- [project.yaml](https://local-review.edspencer.net/reference/project-yaml.md): the full schema, stack selectors, errors and warnings
- [Data directory](https://local-review.edspencer.net/reference/data-directory.md): where data lives, `$LOCAL_REVIEW_HOME`, snapshots
- [prs files](https://local-review.edspencer.net/reference/pr-files.md): PR titles, descriptions, status, branches, GitHub links
- [Comment files](https://local-review.edspencer.net/reference/comment-files.md): the review threads' schema
- [HTTP API](https://local-review.edspencer.net/reference/http-api.md): the server's endpoints
- [CLI](https://local-review.edspencer.net/reference/cli.md): every `local-review` command
- [llms-full.txt](https://local-review.edspencer.net/llms-full.txt): this file followed by the whole agent guide

## Optional

- [PR stacks](https://local-review.edspencer.net/concepts/pr-stacks.md): how commits group into stacks
- [Linked projects](https://local-review.edspencer.net/concepts/linked-projects.md): a project that builds on another
